thread:
matt: Heads-up — new loadtest (replay harness) shows a tail-latency bump after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. 95th and 99th both moved up ~18-25% for the mixed-tenant scenario.

lina: ugh, OK. do you have the perf numbers and the config you used?

matt: quick paste of runtime flags we flipped (from yesterday's PR):
```
--kernel-pick-policy=heuristic_v2
--kernel-size-threshold=384
--continuous-batching=max_delay_ms=6,max_batch=128
--kv-cache=enabled,expire_ms=600000
```
Also ran replay harness with tenant mix: 60% short (<=64), 30% medium (65-512), 10% long (>512).

sajal: saw something similar on my regional tests. suspect the heuristic picks a different GEMM kernel for short-heavy tails which increases per-step overhead. combined with a slightly larger max_delay we may be accumulating badness.

priya: added a quick cpu/gpu flame summary from the profiler (top lines):
```
GPU kernels: conv_gemm_v1 42%
GPU kernels: gemm_dynamic_optimized 18%
Host compute: batch_assembly 12%
KV cache lookup: 9%
Idle/wait: 19%
```
Notice increased host-side wait compared to baseline.

bench-bot: Loadtest 1763012345-rt1 completed: ingress_qps=820, avg_latency=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=420ms, kv_hit_rate=68%

aaron: are these numbers from the replay harness or a synthetic poisson generator? apples-to-apples matters here.

matt: replay harness. earlier synthetic runs (uniform seq=512) looked fine — p95 ~170ms. The replay skew seems to trigger a kernel change and worse batching shapes.

lina: that makes sense. heuristic_v2 switches kernel at seq<=384, so the short requests (<=64) end up grouped and select a small-kernel path that has worse per-call overhead. When mixed with medium requests the runtime oscillates and you get tail amplification.

sajal: two quick mitigations to try: 1) cap effective batch size per-tenant to avoid one tenant hogging big batches, 2) lower max_delay_ms to reduce variance. Example patch we used locally: 
```diff
-continuous-batching=max_delay_ms=6,max_batch=128
+continuous-batching=max_delay_ms=3,max_batch=96,per_tenant_batch_cap=64
```
This brought p99 down ~12% in my small replay.

priya: also check KV cache hit rates — I see kv_hit_rate dropped to 68% in the run, which means more recompute and larger effective latency. Replay harness didn't preserve enough session affinity / cache keys.

matt: confirmed — baseline expected ~93% kv hits on prod-like traffic, but replay didn't preserve cookie/session headers so hit rate collapsed. that's probably a big factor.

bench-bot: New run 1763012500 after patch: ingress_qps=810, avg=69ms, p95=188ms, p99=365ms, kv_hit_rate=86%

aaron: much better. still a gap vs synthetic but closer. For a true apples-to-apples we should: 1) feed the replay harness the original client-side KV keys so cache behavior matches, 2) mirror inter-arrival-time distribution (burstiness), 3) use same seq-length histogram.

lina: agreed. I'll add a replay wrapper that preserves kv_key header and replays arrival gaps. Also will add a config knob to force kernel policy to baseline for comparison.

sajal: i'll run a fairness experiment next: multi-tenant mix with per-tenant caps + weighted queueing (WFQ) to validate no tenant starves when others have long sequences. expecting small loss in peak throughput but much better tail fairness.

priya: for profiling, use this perf hook to capture kernel selection trace and kv stats for a window: 
```bash
./perf-harness --trace kernel_select,kv_hits --duration 120 --out run176301
```
Will give JSON with per-step kernel decisions.

matt: perfect. action items: (1) lina adds wrapper to preserve kv keys + arrival gaps, (2) sajal runs fairness/batchcap experiments with updated cap=64, (3) priya collects perf hooks on next run, (4) i'll validate kernel-selection ablation (heuristic_v2 vs baseline) and open a rollback PR if regression persists.

aaron: +1. let's coordinate a 2hr blocked window on staging so we can collect stable traces.

matt: thanks all — looping back after the runs. :thumbsup:
